changes.to:
## Goal

Add a third mail/calendar backend provider (`provider = "owa"`) that talks to the Microsoft
Outlook web REST API (`https://outlook.office.com/api/v2.0/...`) instead of EWS, so the
`h8` mail/calendar/contacts/availability/rule commands keep working when the EWS headless
auth path (MSAL device-code / Thunderbird public-client recipe) is unusable.

This is a provider-implementation task against the existing seam. Do NOT touch the EWS or
Google providers, the CLI surface, or the service API contract.

## Context / motivation

The `ews` provider authenticates via MSAL with a borrowed public-client app id and an
EWS-only login scope (see `h8-service/h8/oauth/microsoft.py`, the "Thunderbird client-id
EWS recipe"). In tenants that block self-service app registration and headless public-client
flows, that path cannot obtain or refresh a token anymore (`h8 auth status` shows LOGIN: no,
device-code login is refused by Conditional Access). It is not fixable client-side without an
IT-registered app.

Meanwhile the sibling tool `~/byteowlz/cpilot` proved a reliable alternative for such tenants:
capture the `outlook.office.com` bearer token from a logged-in Outlook-web session (its own
managed Chrome profile via CDP). That token carries `Mail.ReadWrite`, `Mail.Send`,
`Calendars.ReadWrite`, `Contacts.ReadWrite`, and the OWA REST `api/v2.0` endpoints return 200s
(mail list/get, calendar, etc.). cpilot already exposes this via `cpilot mail ...` and a raw
`cpilot mail GET /me/...` passthrough. h8 should reuse the SAME auth (call cpilot or read its
token state) rather than reinvent browser capture.

## Scope / seam (read these first)

- `h8-service/h8/providers/base.py` — implement the abstract backends: MailBackend,
  CalendarBackend, ContactsBackend, AvailabilityBackend, DirectoryBackend, SettingsBackend.
- `h8-service/h8/providers/registry.py` — `_FACTORIES` already says "Phase-2 providers
  register here". Add `PROVIDER_OWA` id + `_make_owa` factory.
- `h8-service/h8/providers/ews/__init__.py` — mirror its shape (how it maps provider dicts to
  the normalized item schema the tests assert).
- `h8-service/h8/config.py` — account config gains `provider = "owa"` (token source config).
- Add `h8-service/h8/providers/owa/` package.

## Recommended auth integration

Preferred: depend on cpilot for tokens, do not reimplement browser capture in h8.
- Shell out to `cpilot mail GET <path>` for passthrough, OR read the shared token state at
  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/cpilot/tokens.json` (has `mail_token` + `mail_exp`) and call OWA REST
  directly with `Authorization: Bearer <mail_token>`. If the token is expired, invoke
  `cpilot auth refresh` (which drives the cpilot Chrome silently). Pick one and document it.
- Keep all network/token work off the event loop (registry note: threadpool).

## API notes (learned the hard way, saves you time)

- OWA REST uses **PascalCase** props on list/select (e.g. `ReceivedDateTime`, `From`,
  `Subject`, `IsRead`, `Id`) — NOT Graph camelCase.
- `From`/`ToRecipients` are inline on the message; they are NOT `$expand`-able (EWS/Graph
  habit breaks here).
- `?orderby=ReceivedDateTime desc`, `$select`, `$top` work as expected.
- `sendMail` body shape: `{"Message":{"Subject","Body":{"ContentType","Content"},
  "ToRecipients":[{"EmailAddress":{"Address"}}]},"SaveToSentItems":true}`.
- Endpoint base: `https://outlook.office.com/api/v2.0`.

## Capability parity / expected gaps (set expectations, raise BackendNotSupported)

Map what OWA REST supports; for the rest raise `BackendNotSupported(capability=...)` so the
CLI degrades cleanly. Known-tricky: attachments (list/download), RSVP/invites, inbox rule
writes, GAL/directory resolve, resource (room/car) availability. Availability/free-busy may
need a Graph `getschedule` call (different audience/token than the OWA token) — document if
that command can't be served by the OWA token alone.

## Proof of positive outcome

- New provider passes the shared contract tests in `tests/test_providers_contract.py` with a
  recorded/faked OWA HTTP fixture (no live network in CI). Add an OWA fixture set mirroring the
  EWS/Google ones.
- `h8 config` account with `provider = "owa"` resolves a backend via the registry.
- Smoke (manual, documented, NOT in CI): `h8 mail ls`, `h8 mail get <id>`, `h8 calendar ls`
  return live data against a licensed M365 mailbox via the cpilot token. Show trimmed output in
  the PR/issue comment; redact any third-party mailbox identifiers/emails.
- EWS and Google provider tests still pass unchanged (`just test`).

## Non-goals

- No changes to the EWS provider or its MSAL code.
- No new browser/token-capture implementation in h8 (reuse cpilot).
- No CLI flag surface changes beyond what the provider registry needs.
